podcast.title: Mid-60s North American Phenomenon
podcast.body: Throughout the mid-1960s, garage bands proliferated in garages across North America. These groups were often characterized by their rough and ragged sound, sometimes incorporating risqué material. "Throughout the mid-60s, bands popped up in garages all across North America."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Rebellious Image and "Punks" Label
podcast.body: Some garage bands adopted a rebellious image, wearing leather jackets reminiscent of James Dean. Some observers at the time used the term "punks" to describe this look, an early association of the word with a musical subculture. "Some observers said these jackets made them look like punks."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Underground Popularity
podcast.body: While a few garage bands achieved hit singles, most remained underground. They found popularity with a specific type of music fan who preferred their music "rough and raw and real." "They remained underground, popular with a certain type of music band, the kind that liked their music rough and raw and real."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
